detailed_rationale:
Capillary Technologies is a recently-listed loyalty/martech SaaS provider (customer loyalty, engagement and personalization platforms for retail/consumer brands), having raised roughly Rs 877.5 crore via IPO. FY26 full-year results showed consolidated revenue up 23% YoY to Rs 734.6 crore and consolidated PAT up 295% YoY to Rs 52.4 crore -- a headline that looks strong, but standalone PAT actually fell to just Rs 2.9 crore due to acquisition-related costs, indicating the consolidated profit jump is being driven by scope/accounting effects around M&A rather than a clean, comparable improvement in the core business. Q1 FY27 results were not yet available as of this review (earnings call scheduled for the day after this review).

The quant data is a genuine, current-period concern, not stale: ROE of -14.0% and ROCE of -1.0% are both negative, meaning the business is not yet earning an adequate return on its capital base despite the reported revenue and consolidated-PAT growth -- quality score of just 2.9 is the lowest in this entire batch of names reviewed. As a recently-listed company, price-history coverage is also thin (12- and 24-month returns are not available), which limits how much confidence can be placed in the momentum-based components of the quant score, but does not change the fact that core profitability metrics are negative today.

At a PE of ~63x, the market is paying a rich multiple for a business that, on a comparable (standalone, non-M&A-inflated) basis, is barely profitable and has negative return on capital. Fast revenue growth in a genuine SaaS niche is a real positive, but it does not offset negative ROE/ROCE and a valuation this full for a company with limited public operating history -- there is no basis to override the quant Sell.
recommendation_rationale: ROE (-14.0%) and ROCE (-1.0%) are both negative, and the large consolidated-PAT jump this year appears driven substantially by M&A/accounting scope effects rather than a clean underlying margin improvement (standalone PAT was just Rs 2.9 crore). Combined with a rich ~63x PE and very limited public trading history to validate execution, there is no basis for a rescue to Hold.
summary: Capillary Technologies, a recently-listed loyalty and customer-engagement software company, is growing revenue at a healthy pace, but its return on equity and capital employed are both currently negative, and a large part of this year's reported profit jump appears to reflect acquisition-related accounting effects rather than a clean underlying improvement. With limited public trading history and a rich valuation for a business not yet earning positive returns on capital, we would not hold this position.
positive_para: Revenue grew 23% YoY to Rs 734.6 crore in FY26, and the company operates in a genuine, growing SaaS niche (loyalty, engagement and personalization software for consumer brands) with a cash-rich balance sheet (D/E just 0.05) following its recent IPO, giving it runway to invest in growth without near-term financing pressure.
negative_para: ROE (-14.0%) and ROCE (-1.0%) are both negative, meaning the business is not yet earning an adequate return on its capital, and the standalone entity's profit was only Rs 2.9 crore for the full year after acquisition-related costs -- the much larger consolidated PAT jump appears driven by M&A/accounting scope effects rather than a clean underlying margin improvement. As a recently-listed company there is limited public track record to validate sustained execution, and the ~63x PE leaves little room for error.
reverse_dcf_judgment: With ROE and ROCE both negative, there is no positive current return on capital to anchor a reverse-DCF; a ~63x PE on a business that is only marginally profitable on a standalone basis after acquisition costs implies the market is pricing several years of both revenue growth and a genuine margin inflection that has not yet been demonstrated in comparable, non-M&A-affected results.
